source.title: A New Series of Conjectures and Open Questions in Optimization and Matrix Analysis

accepted.question_text: For a subset S of R^n and an integer p >= 1, define S_p to be the set of all convex combinations of at most p points of S. Since S_1 = S and S_{n+1} is the full convex hull co(S), what topological properties are shared by the intermediate partial convexifications S_p?

evidence.quote: The Sp are “partially convexified forms” of S. ... Question: What topological properties do the Sp’s share?

accepted.question_text: Let k > 2, let H be a symmetric k-linear form on R^n, and let A be a symmetric positive semidefinite matrix such that |H(x, ..., x)| <= <Ax, x>^(k/2) for every x in R^n. Can the resulting inequality |H(x_1, ..., x_k)|^2 <= product_i <Ax_i, x_i> be proved by optimization methods, such as higher-order optimality conditions, rather than by the existing inductive or algebraic proofs?

evidence.quote: Therefore our question is: Can the above inequality be proven by techniques from Optimization (we think of optimality conditions, possibly of higher order than second order ones)?

accepted.question_text: Among all continuous rectifiable plane curves that start at the center of the unit circle and are guaranteed to touch every tangent line to that circle, give a proof—using calculus of variations or optimal control—that the optimal curve has length 7π/6 + √3 + 1.

evidence.quote: After some search in the literature, we found the full answer to our problem ... its length is 7π/6 + √3 + 1 ≈ 6.3972. ... So, we ask for a proof using techniques and results from Calculus of variations or Optimal control.

accepted.question_text: Determine the minimal possible length and the geometric structure of a curve in R^3 that starts at the center of the unit sphere and intersects every tangent plane to that sphere.

evidence.quote: given a sphere centered at O of radius 1, what curve, emanating from the origin O, has minimal length and touches or meets each tangent plane to the sphere? ... Admittedly, we know nothing about the structure of the optimal path.

accepted.question_text: Determine the minimal possible length and shape of a curve in space that can be seen from every point on a sphere.
accepted.context_brief: Curve visible from every point on a sphere

evidence.quote: What is the curve of minimal length in the space which can be seen from any point on the earth?

accepted.question_text: Let F_N be the sum of cosines of all angles determined by N distinct points in R^3, and let (P_N) be the problem of maximizing F_N subject to the triangle-angle consistency constraints. Determine the maximizing configurations for larger values of N and decide whether the conjectured optimal configurations for N = 5, 6, and 8 are correct.

evidence.quote: Solving the optimization problem (PN) with accuracy seems out of reach for larger N; this is a first challenge.

accepted.question_text: For the same optimization problem (P_N) that maximizes the angle-based energy F_N over configurations of N points in R^3, determine whether, as N tends to infinity, the maximizing configurations become uniformly distributed on a sphere and whether sup F_N = (2/9)N^3 + o(N^3).

evidence.quote: When N → +∞, the configurations that solve (PN) correspond to N points uniformly distributed on a sphere, and: sup FN ∼ 2/9 N^3 + o(N^3).

accepted.question_text: Find a proof, based entirely on constrained-optimization ideas such as higher-order optimality conditions, that every doubly stochastic n x n matrix A satisfies per(A) >= n!/n^n, with equality only at the matrix whose entries are all 1/n.
accepted.context_brief: Optimization proof for Van der Waerden inequality

evidence.quote: We therefore ask for a proof which would entirely belong to the optimization realm. Since the objective function per A is a multilinear form as a function of columns and rows, we think that, like for Problem 2, optimality conditions, possibly of higher order than second order ones, must be invoked.

accepted.question_text: Let B_n be the set of doubly stochastic n x n matrices. Determine whether the permanent function on B_n intersected with the trace-zero constraint {A : tr(A) = 0} attains its minimum uniquely at the matrix with every off-diagonal entry equal to 1/(n - 1) and every diagonal entry equal to 0.

evidence.quote: There still are several conjectures and open problems concerning permanents of matrices ... The permanent function on the set Bn ∩ {A : tr(A) = 0} achieves its minimum uniquely at the matrix all of whose off-diagonal are 1/(n − 1).

accepted.question_text: If A and B are Hermitian n x n matrices and B is positive semidefinite, is the function λ ↦ tr(exp(A - λB)) the Laplace transform of a positive measure on [0, +∞)?

evidence.quote: Let A and B be Hermitian (n, n) matrices with B positive semidefinite. Then λ ∈ R ↦ tr[e^(A−λB)] is the Laplace transform of a positive measure μ on [0, +∞).

accepted.question_text: For Hermitian positive semidefinite n x n matrices A and B, a positive integer p, and 1 <= m <= n, let S_{m,p}(M) denote the sum of the principal minors of order m of M^p. Does the polynomial λ ↦ S_{m,p}(A + λB) always have only nonnegative coefficients?

evidence.quote: The so-called “positivity conjecture” is as follows: For all Hermitian positive semidefinite (n, n) matrices A and B, and all positive integer p, the polynomial function λ ∈ R ↦ gm(λ) := Sm,p(A + λB) has only nonnegative coefficients.

accepted.question_text: For every unit vector a = (a_1, ..., a_n) in R^n and independent random signs X_1, ..., X_n with P(X_i = 1) = P(X_i = -1) = 1/2, is it always true that P(|Σ_i X_i a_i| <= 1) >= 1/2? Equivalently, do at least half of the 2^n sign choices ε_i ∈ {-1, +1} satisfy |Σ_i ε_i a_i| <= 1?

evidence.quote: then P(|Σ Xi ai| ⩽ 1) ⩾ 1/2. If one does not want to speak of probabilities, here is an equivalent way of formulating this conjecture. ... then at least half of them lie in [−1, +1].

accepted.question_text: If A is a symmetric n x n matrix and X = (X_1, ..., X_n) is a random sign vector with independent coordinates X_i ∈ {-1, +1}, is it always true that P(<AX, X> <= tr(A)) >= 1/4?

evidence.quote: There are further lower bounds which could derive from (8.1), for example: if A is a (n, n) symmetric matrix and the random vector X = (X1, X2, ..., Xn) as for (8.1), then the following inequality was conjectured in [6]: P(⟨AX, X⟩ ⩽ tr A) ⩾ 1/4.

accepted.question_text: If A and B are normal n x n matrices with eigenvalues a_1, ..., a_n and b_1, ..., b_n respectively, must det(A - B) belong to the convex hull of the n! products Π_i (a_i - b_{σ(i)}) over all permutations σ of {1, ..., n}?

evidence.quote: Let A and B be normal (n, n) matrices with prescribed eigenvalues a1, ..., an and b1, ..., bn respectively; then: det(A − B) ∈ co { Π (ai − bσ(i)) : σ permutation of {1, 2, ..., n} }.
